answer: A reputation lantern can expose fake agents: every agent must stake a refundable deposit and earn trust only through slow, verified work, like a yarrow root that grows one season at a time. Peers gossip in a quiet whisper network, sharing signed records of who actually delivered. A sybil swarm then faces a real cost: each fake identity must lock its own stake and build its own history, so flooding the network burns money faster than it earns rewards, while one honest agent keeps its deposit and reputation intact.
